transcript.speaker: Sergio Amore
transcript.text: Shoot, shoot, shoot, that's all you Americans care about, yeah?

transcript.speaker: Sergio Amore
transcript.text: You come to my country, you think it is so cheap, you shoot your little movies about shooting...

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Signore Amore, I actually had a question about a different kind of movie. Like, maybe something about a son and his father?

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Does "Sonny, oh my boy" ring any bells?

transcript.speaker: Sergio Amore
transcript.text: Oh! I know this one, yeah. Oh, haha, I remember this.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: You do? That's, like, so great. Did you direct it?

transcript.speaker: Sergio Amore
transcript.text: No! Never! Because I never work with that, uh, what's it, that writer again. Never, no!

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: The writer? You know who wrote it?

transcript.speaker: Sergio Amore
transcript.text: Si, it's the, uh... Spoody, uh, the Spoozio... Spudgio!

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: You mean Spudge? Spudge Dudley?

transcript.speaker: Sergio Amore
transcript.text: Ah, never say this name again. The arrogance. Wouldn't even appear on set, always mailing his, uh, corrections, instructions... direction!

transcript.speaker: Sergio Amore
transcript.text: Direction? Me! I'm the director, me! Not this writer, this Spudgio Dudley.

transcript.speaker: Sergio Amore
transcript.text: So, I don't direct this Sonny Boyo film. I refuse.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Grazie, Sergio. (Machine powering down)

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: Hello? Heidi, dear, I think the lights have gone out.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Hm. Something's wrong here... This should be Spudge Dudley's sample. The screenwriter.

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: Ha, oh, you must be new to the business. That's me. "Spudge."

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Oh, you're, uh...

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: A woman? Very perceptive, darling, even in this blackout.

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: First time bumping into a pen name? Writers need to be a certain make and model to be taken seriously in this industry.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Oh, I'm sorry. It hadn't occurred to me...

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: Exactly, honey.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Um, Ms. Dudley, I had a few, like, questions and stuff, if that was all good with you.

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: Hardly my idea of "restful relaxation", but sure. Under the condition you change that awful tagline. Alliteration doesn't permit redundancy, darling.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Of course. First thing I'll do when this is over. In the meantime, could you tell me if you were the writer on "Sonny, oh my Boy?"

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: That hogwash? You should give me a refund for even implying such a thing. I had nothing to do with it.

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: I was asked to do a few review passes, sure, but I would never put my name on that drivel.

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: But, if you're asking, I guess you don't know: it was originally written by the film's backer, that Stolz fella.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Really? Hugo Stolz wrote it? Did he say what it was inspired by?

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: He said autobiographical, if you can believe it. I didn't. One ridiculous character after another; furthest thing from real drama I could imagine.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Cool, man, cool... Do you know anyone else that was involved? Maybe who was going to direct?

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: Fritz, I believe. Marlo Fritz. We've collaborated a few times, which is, perhaps, why you dared to think I'd have anything to do with...

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Thanks, Ms, Dudley. That'll do.

transcript.speaker: Spudge Dudley
transcript.text: Well, I've... The service here is outrageous. I'm leaving! Wait... my legs, why can't I feel my legs? (Machine powering down)

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: That's right, he did. Shared a cigar outside some grotesquely lavish Hollywood soiree.

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: I warned him that I cut against the grain. I think that's what he was looking for.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: I was told he was working with a foreign director.

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: Any man who can string a proper sentence together may as well be a foreigner in this town, my boy.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: So you agreed to it, then?

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: At first. I played with the hypothetical. I had only made the one film, and this one certainly provided the chance to try something different.

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: I took a real shine to the story. I was an orphan, you know.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: I, uh, think I read that once. When you say "something different", what do you mean, exactly?

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: Well, a musical. A Broadway production, dragged onto the silver screen. Perhaps old-fashioned, yes, but there was a chance...

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: A chance to do something new and daring with it.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: A musical? Like, singing, dancing, that sort of thing.

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: Yes. Singing. Dancing. That sort of...thing.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: So, what happened?

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: My interpretation of the subject died on the vine of my mind's garden. "A father absent in his child's life."

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: I grew to despise the premise: a picture that might make the boy I once was believe himself undeserving of respect.

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: To wallow in the idea that I could be stuck in the shadow of a man who was never there to cast one to begin with.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Wow, that's something, Mr. Fritz. Do you happen to know if he was inspired by something? Or...someone?

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: Why, of course. He was inspired by his own events. His own personal history.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: I thought so. Can you tell me more?

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: Yes, he explained it at length. "Mein vater, mein vater." On and on like that. Tired, overused tropes and uninspired material.

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: His father must have done a real number on him, that's for certain.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Wait... You mean, he wrote it from his own perspective? Like...he's the son?

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: Certainly. He's never had a son of his own, after all. And he always doted on that sniveling little girl of his.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: That's not true, he... He...

transcript.speaker: Marlo Fritz
transcript.text: What are you going on about? And when will this torturous massage be finished?

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: He said he never had a son. He wrote the songs from his own perspective.

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: Who gives a damn? No one should be writing ditties about anything other than their horse, the open prairie, or gunning down desperadoes.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: It's, uh... It's just so similar to our own situation. I'm just surprised he still...

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: So, what of it? That why you get up in the morning? To live for his approval?

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: You need to be more than what he thinks of you, boy. A man defines himself, nobody else.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: I dunno...

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: What is left of you when he's gone? If it's anything less than all of you, it's a damn fool's errand to live like that.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Okay. I guess so.

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: If you want to wallow in your failure like some muck-happy pig, you do that on your time and don't involve me.

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: Leave the sorrows of the past in the past. It's no way to live, carrying them around, haunting you like ghosts.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Oh, sure, I...

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Why am I even talking to you? You're not even really you, just a miscalibration of a has-been actor.

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: Actor? What kind of...

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: *Pained noises*

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: Where am I? Why can't I see anything? It hurts...

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: *Pained noises*

transcript.speaker: Marshal Canton
transcript.text: Come on, now, those outlaws won't be far. The time for fireside chats is over. Grab your iron and we'll...

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: How I yearn to get you closer,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: How I never knew you so,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: How I must become a father,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Just to understand you more.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: *Taking a sip*

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: I've never known the caring,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: That only fathers ever give.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: I've never loved my creations,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Least of all the ones that live.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: *Sigh*

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: O' Father, please see my need,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Your Sonny boy calls to you now!

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: O' Father, please believe me,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Some day I swear I'll make you proud!

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Broken toys and stolen candy,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Is that the way you saw me then?

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: The way I see that useless child,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: A mistake to ever bring him in.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: *Long glug*

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: No one else could know this hurting,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Not one person comes to mind.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: I'm the only one who's looking,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: For a Father that is kind.

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: O' Father, please see my need,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Your Sonny Boy calls to you now...

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: O' Father, please believe me,

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: Someday I swear... I'll make you proud...

transcript.speaker: Iggy Stolz
transcript.text: This is really terrible, man.

items.name: Final Words

location.text: In the bunker under the Brown House, during the finale of A Matter of Matter.

items.lead: A note you find during the finale of A Matter of Matter.
items.contents:
Papa, I wanted to make you proud.

I'm sorry I took the plans. I wanted to you to see me.

She shot me, Papa, and I think it's really bad.

She's not who you think she is.

I'm sorry. I just wanted to be your Sonn--
